summary: Hand-verified corrections applied on 2026-10-24 on top of the 2026-10-23 snapshot. The NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP service could not be reached from the build workspace, so values were read from the Archive's system overview pages, NASA Science catalogue pages and Wikipedia; each correction records its source URL in tools/data/corrections.json.

sources.NASA-EA: NASA Exoplanet Archive system overview pages (exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/overview/...): distances (sy_dist), parameter solutions and mass type (Mp vs Mp sin i); read 2026-10-24
sources.Rosenthal2021: Rosenthal et al. 2021, ApJS 255, 8 - California Legacy Survey (51 Peg b M sin i = 147 Earth masses)
sources.Mallorquin2024: Mallorquín et al. 2024, A&A 685, A90 - AU Mic b and c masses (NASA default set)
sources.ZapateroOsorio2026: Zapatero Osorio et al. 2026 - TOI-198 b (NASA Exoplanet Archive solution)
sources.Philipot2023: Philipot et al. 2023, A&A 670, A65 - Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry + RV true masses (HIP 70849 b, BD-21 397 c, HD 75302 b)
sources.Feng2022: Feng et al. 2022, ApJS 262, 21 - 3D selection of 167 substellar companions (astrometric true masses)
sources.Han2018: Han et al. 2018, AJ 155, 26 (arXiv:1811.08625) - DE CVn eclipse-timing companion
sources.Nowak2020: Nowak et al. 2020, A&A 642, L2 - GRAVITY detection of beta Pic c
sources.Maire2019: Maire et al. 2019, A&A 624, A118 - 51 Eri b orbit
sources.Brogi2012: Brogi et al. 2012, Nature 486, 502 - tau Boo b true mass

sources.Limbach2025: Limbach et al. 2025, ApJL 984, L28 - JWST thermal emission of WD 1856+534 b (model mass)

gj-1214/Gliese 1214.verified: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GJ_1214 (0.1820 solar masses); makes a = 0.01505 AU consistent with P = 1.5804 d

notes: Found by radial velocity and does not transit, so only its minimum mass (M sin i) is known and its radius is an estimate (NASA lists 1.26 Jupiter radii, estimate).

notes: The Open Exoplanet Catalogue gave a = 0.0396 AU, which does not fit the 3.12-day period; NASA's 0.02661 AU does.

hip-12961-b.verified: https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/hip-12961-b/ (orbital radius 0.25 AU, period 57.4 d, radius 1.18 RJ estimate)

notes: Orbit, mass and radius from Zapatero Osorio et al. 2026; the Open Exoplanet Catalogue's a = 0.10 AU did not fit the 10.2-day period.
toi-198-b.verified: https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/overview/TOI-198 (a 0.0675 au, P 10.215213 d, Mp 3.17, Rp 1.36, M* 0.417)

notes: Circumbinary: it orbits both the white dwarf (0.51 solar masses) and the red dwarf (0.41). Eclipse timing gives only a minimum mass (M sin i, about 12 Jupiter masses).
Its orbit (5.75 ± 2.02 AU, 11.2 years) is around the combined 0.92 solar-mass binary, not the white dwarf alone; with that mass Kepler’s law gives about 4.9 AU, inside the quoted uncertainty.

notes: The Open Exoplanet Catalogue had placeholder-looking values (P = 10,000 d, a = 10 AU, 9 Jupiter masses); replaced with Philipot et al. 2023 (4.5 Jupiter masses, 3.99 AU, 10 years).
hip-70849-b.verified: https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/overview/HIP%2070849 (Philipot 2023: Mp 1430 Earth, a 3.99 au, P 3649 d, e 0.65, i 96; An 2025 agrees: 4.55 MJ, 4.037 au)

notes: The atlas previously showed 57 Earth masses, which is Plavchan et al. 2020's upper limit, not a measurement. Published radial-velocity masses range from about 6 to 20 Earth masses; the NASA default is 8.99 (Mallorquín et al. 2024).
au-mic-b.verified: https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/overview/AU%20Mic (Plavchan 2020: Mp sin i < 57 upper limit; Mallorquin 2024: 8.99 Earth, 4.79 R, a 0.070, P 8.463446); https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/au-microscopii-b/ (8.99 Earth masses)

notes: The atlas previously showed 13.8 Jupiter masses, which is Vanderburg et al. 2020's upper limit. JWST thermal emission (Limbach et al. 2025) gives about 5.2 Jupiter masses from cooling models.
